anchors.description: Full height of the tall light-wood corner cabinet (armoire with mirrored door) in the right foreground, measured along its front-left vertical corner edge from the floor contact to the top corner of the cabinet body just below the crown.
anchors.visible_evidence: The light-wood corner cabinet stands on the tile floor at right; its front-left corner edge is fully visible from the floor contact at (424,449) up to the top corner at (455,50), where the body meets the crown. The cabinet top sits just below the ceiling. Both endpoints lie on the same rigid vertical corner edge, so their 3-D separation is the cabinet's height.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Identified by appearance as a residential tall corner cabinet/armoire; no brand or spec is legible. Category heights for such cabinets are about 2.0-2.4 m, and the exact crown/body boundary at the top adds a few centimetres of uncertainty.

anchors.description: Width along the top edge of the pale paneled interior door at the back right of the room, from its hinge-side top corner to its free-edge top corner.
anchors.visible_evidence: Behind the dining chairs a pale paneled interior door sits in a dark frame; its top edge is unoccluded between the hinge-side corner at (394,152) and the free-edge corner at (438,158). The visible leaf proportions (about 2.5-2.8:1 height to width) match a standard residential interior door.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: The door is roughly 8 m away and its lower part is hidden by chair backs; whether the leaf is open or closed cannot be confirmed, but the top-edge span equals the leaf width either way. US interior door widths fall in 28-36 in (0.71-0.91 m).
